verdict.summary: You can create a HubSpot OAuth app with the CLI and connect your own account in under an hour. Once you sign the Acceptable Use Policy, up to 25 accounts can install a Marketplace-distributed app without review (10 for private apps), but each one first sees a risk-confirmation dialog. Unlimited installs require a Marketplace listing, which needs 3 active installs from unaffiliated accounts and a manual review by HubSpot.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-2 hours to reach a working app; 1-2 days to prepare the Marketplace listing (legal pages, setup docs, scope cleanup)
verdict.approval_wait: None for your own account or the first 25 installs. A Marketplace listing gets an initial review within 10 business days, and HubSpot says the full review should take no more than 60 days from when it shares feedback. Before you can submit, you also need 3 active installs from unaffiliated accounts.

gates.name: Developer test accounts (before signing the Acceptable Use Policy)
gates.unlocks: You can create the app, get the client ID and secret, and complete OAuth in your developer test accounts.
limits: Until you sign the Acceptable Use Policy, the app can be installed only in developer test accounts
The installing user must be a Super Admin or have Marketplace Access, plus the permission for each scope group the app requests

gates.name: Unlisted Marketplace-distributed app / privately distributed app
gates.unlocks: Real HubSpot customer accounts can install the app without review.
limits: Marketplace-distributed OAuth apps on platform 2025.2 or later can be installed in at most 25 accounts until listed
Privately distributed OAuth apps can be installed in at most 10 allowlisted accounts (developer test accounts don't count toward this)
Unreviewed third-party apps show a confirmation dialog. For an unverified app, users must type 'I accept the risk' before they can connect
Rate limit for publicly distributed apps: 110 requests per 10 seconds per installing account
gates.time_to_reach: Same day (sign the AUP; verifying your domain is optional)

gates.name: Listed on the HubSpot App Marketplace
gates.unlocks: Unlimited installs, and the 25-install cap is removed.
limits: Needs at least 3 active installs: production accounts unaffiliated with your organization, with successful app activity in the last 30 days
Only one app can be in the approval queue at a time. Any extra submission is automatically rejected
Listings with incomplete fields stay in Draft mode
gates.time_to_reach: Initial review within 10 business days of submission. HubSpot says the full process should take no more than 60 days from when it shares feedback. You also need time beforehand to collect 3 active unaffiliated installs

steps.title: Create a HubSpot developer account
steps.detail: Sign up for a HubSpot developer account using the signup link on HubSpot's developer site. Your apps and developer test accounts live in this account.

steps.title: Create the app project with the HubSpot CLI
steps.detail: Follow HubSpot's 'Create a new app using the CLI' guide to create a project with an app component. When the CLI asks, choose Marketplace distribution if any outside accounts will install the app, or restrict installs to specific HubSpot accounts for private distribution.
gotchas: Private apps can be installed in at most 10 allowlisted accounts. Marketplace distribution allows 25 installs before listing and unlimited installs after.
The CLI must be authenticated to your developer account, so you need to grant that access first.

steps.title: Set the redirect URL and scopes in app-hsmeta.json
steps.detail: In the app's top-level app-hsmeta.json, set redirectUrls to the Composio callback URL. List scopes in the auth block as required, optional or conditionally required. Then run hs project upload to deploy the changes.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: The redirect URL must use https in production and must be a domain, not an IP address. Plain http is allowed only for localhost.

Every scope marked as required must appear in the authorization URL's scope parameter, or the authorization page shows an error. Your Composio auth config's scopes must match the app's required scopes.
Optional scopes are dropped silently if the account doesn't have access to that tool. Check the token to see which scopes were actually granted.

steps.title: Trim the scope list to what your agent uses
steps.detail: Composio's default HubSpot scope list is broad and includes settings.users.write and crm.import. Keep only the scopes your agent actually calls. Move scopes that only some customers need to optional or conditionally required.
gotchas: Installing users need the permission for every scope group you request. For example, crm.import requires the Import permission.
Marketplace reviewers compare requested scopes against your last 30 days of API logs and ask you to remove scopes you don't use.

steps.title: Copy the client credentials into Composio
steps.detail: In the developer account, open your project, go to Project Components > your app > Auth tab, and copy the Client ID and Client secret from the Client credentials section. Paste them into a Composio HubSpot auth config that uses your own OAuth app.
gotchas: You can rotate the client secret from the Auth tab. If you do, update Composio right away.

steps.title: Run a test connection from a developer test account
steps.detail: Start a Composio connection and authorize with a developer test account as a Super Admin. Then check Development > Monitoring > Logs in the developer account for the install, grant and token exchange events.
gotchas: The app shows up as a Connected App only after the code has been exchanged for tokens. The code is single-use and has a short exchange window.
A bad client ID can still return a normal-looking HubSpot OAuth page (HTTP 200), so confirm success in the logs instead of relying on the page.

steps.title: Sign the Acceptable Use Policy
steps.detail: Review and sign HubSpot's Acceptable Use Policy for the app. Until you do, the app can be installed only in developer test accounts.

steps.title: Verify your domain to reduce the install warning
steps.detail: Add the TXT DNS record HubSpot provides to verify your domain. Unverified apps show a warning banner, and users must type 'I accept the risk' before connecting. A developer account can have only one verified domain, and all apps in the account share it.
gotchas: Deleting the verified domain brings the install warning back.
Since March 23, 2026, apps that HubSpot's Marketplace quality team hasn't reviewed still show a confirmation dialog during install.

steps.title: Onboard test users within the install cap
steps.detail: Have pilot customers connect through your app, or allowlist their accounts if you chose private distribution. Watch the install count: 25 for unlisted Marketplace apps, 10 for private apps.
gotchas: Legacy public apps with more than 25 installs get the 25-install cap enforced automatically when migrated to the new developer platform.
Throttle API calls to stay under 110 requests per 10 seconds per account. The API limit increase add-on does not raise this limit.

steps.title: Get 3 active installs from unaffiliated accounts
steps.detail: Before you submit a listing, at least 3 unique production HubSpot accounts unaffiliated with your organization must show successful app activity within the past 30 days.

steps.title: Prepare listing assets
steps.detail: Draft and publish live public URLs that HubSpot's crawler can reach: Terms of Service, Privacy Policy, setup documentation and the install button URL. Add a support contact and shared-data documentation that matches your requested scopes. Do not combine HubSpot's name with your app name or logo.
gotchas: Incomplete listing fields keep the listing in Draft mode.
OAuth must be the app's only authorization method, and the app needs a single public app ID and client ID.

steps.title: Submit the Marketplace listing
steps.detail: Submit the listing for review from your developer account. Submit only one app at a time.
gotchas: Any other submission made while one is pending is automatically rejected.

steps.title: Wait for Ecosystem Quality review
steps.detail: HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team aims to finish an initial review within 10 business days. HubSpot says the full review and feedback process should take no more than 60 days from when it shares feedback. A third-party blog estimates 2-4 weeks for most submissions in 2026. Once the listing is approved, the 25-install cap is removed.
steps.est_time: 10 business days for the initial review

requirements.item: HTTPS redirect URL on a domain (not an IP address)
requirements.detail: Plain http is allowed only for localhost testing. Set the URL in redirectUrls in app-hsmeta.json.
The installing user must be a Super Admin or have Marketplace Access, plus the permission for each scope group the app requests.
Required before the app can be installed outside developer test accounts.
Optional for installs, but it removes the unverified-app warning. One verified domain per developer account. Required for certification.
Production accounts outside your organization with successful activity in the last 30 days.

requirements.item: Live Terms of Service, Privacy Policy, setup docs, install URL, support contact and shared-data documentation
requirements.detail: The URLs must be live and reachable by HubSpot's crawler, and the shared-data documentation must match the requested scopes.

requirements.item: Scopes limited to what the app uses; OAuth as the only auth method
requirements.detail: Remove unused scopes. Make scopes that only some customers need conditionally required or optional.

Requires 6+ months listed, 60 active installs, a demo video, a security questionnaire, a verified domain, an API success rate above 95%, and a fully automated authorization code flow. You cannot ask users to paste codes or tokens.

scopes.effect: The installing user must have the Import permission, or the install fails for them. Drop this scope unless your agent imports data.
Included in Composio's defaults. These are admin-level scopes. Reviewers remove scopes that don't show up in your API logs, so drop them unless your agent manages users.

scopes.scope: Sensitive Data / Highly Sensitive Data scopes
scopes.effect: Marketplace-bound apps must request these from HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team, which allowlists them for testing. The installing account needs an Enterprise subscription. App card apps cannot use them.
Dropped silently when the installing account doesn't have access to the tool. Check which scopes were granted on the token.

blockers.symptom: Authorization page shows a scope error
blockers.cause: A scope marked as required in the app isn't in the authorization URL's scope parameter.
blockers.fix: Make the scopes in your Composio auth config match the required scopes in app-hsmeta.json exactly, or mark the extra scopes as optional.

blockers.symptom: A user can't install the app
blockers.cause: The user isn't a Super Admin, or lacks Marketplace Access or the permission for a requested scope group (for example, Import for crm.import).
blockers.fix: Have a Super Admin install the app, or remove scopes that need permissions the user doesn't have.

blockers.symptom: New installs fail after 25 accounts (or 10 for private apps)
blockers.cause: Install caps for unlisted Marketplace apps and private apps.
blockers.fix: Get the app listed on the Marketplace to remove the 25-install cap. A private app stays capped at 10 allowlisted accounts.

blockers.symptom: Users see a warning and must type 'I accept the risk'
blockers.cause: The app isn't on a verified domain or hasn't been reviewed by the Marketplace quality team.
blockers.fix: Verify your domain with a TXT record, and get the app listed.

blockers.symptom: 429 errors / certification feedback about burst limits
blockers.cause: More than about 100-110 requests per 10 seconds per account.
blockers.fix: Throttle per account, and refresh tokens before they expire instead of waiting for a 401.

blockers.symptom: Listing stuck in Draft or submission auto-rejected
blockers.cause: Listing fields are incomplete, or another app is already in the approval queue.
blockers.fix: Complete every listing field with live URLs, and submit one app at a time.

composio.note: Composio's managed HubSpot app is the quickest way to prototype. Its default scope list is broad and includes admin-level settings.users write access and crm.import. Register your own app when you need your own branding and client credentials, a narrower scope list, or control over install caps and Marketplace listing. An unlisted Marketplace app tops out at 25 installs and a private app at 10. When you switch, paste the exact callback URL from your Composio auth config into redirectUrls, and make sure the auth config's scopes match the app's required scopes.

open_questions: Access and refresh token lifetimes (the actual expires_in value) were not captured.
Composio's managed HubSpot app: whether it is Marketplace-listed, its install cap, and which redirect URL it uses (v1 auth-apps/add vs v3 toolkits/auth/callback) were not verified.
Whether a basic Marketplace listing (as opposed to certification) needs a demo video or security questionnaire was not confirmed.
Whether a free developer account is enough to publish was not stated.
How to qualify as a Solutions Partner, which reportedly raises the private app install cap to 100, was not researched.
Whether changing required scopes forces existing users to re-authorize is supported only by a community post (f37).
